Pixel Blade · the mark · act five

The mark was in the wrong layer.

Everything else in this brand has been dimensional since the material round — surfaces, raking light, things that are made. The logo was the only piece still being solved as though it were a printer's problem from 1974. You called it: flat, two-dimensional, logo-creation-101. Here is the correction.

The move

A mark is not artwork. It is a die.

The flat vector is the tool, not the deliverable. It gets pressed into something. Same geometry every time — nothing below was drawn by hand, and nothing was drawn by an image model.

Bronze foil on dark construction paper. Your words, more or less exactly.

Six materials, one geometry

If it doesn't work flat, strike it.

What this settles

The geometry was never the problem.

Last round I spent an entire pass trying to make one hairline in the page ground imply a fold in the crane's wing, and told you honestly that it read as a folded bird rather than unmistakably a paper crane.

Look at the cut-paper version. The fold reads instantly — because it is a real edge throwing a real shadow, not a line pretending to be one. Your reference with the rendered orizuru is the proof: that crane reads as folded paper because adjacent planes sit at different angles to one light and land at different values. Nothing is drawn. The fold is where two values meet.

Which means the mark was being asked to be a folded object in a medium that has no folds. That is a medium problem, and you diagnosed it in one line.

Enforced in code, not remembered

brand/strike.py

Seven modes, any mark, any material, repeatably. Rerun make-struck.sh and the whole set follows the geometry. The rules that make it look real rather than rendered are constants in the file:

  • One raking light, low

    Upper left, shallow. Already the brand's rule. Two sources is a bug. The lower the light, the longer the shoulder, the more physical the result.

  • Specular is one near-white line

    Never gold, never a bloom around the whole silhouette. That bloom is a bevel filter and it reads as amateur from across a room. Metal that glows all the way round its own outline is plastic.

  • Relief needs faked occlusion

    A flat raised face has the same normal as the flat field beside it, so directional light alone renders them identically and the mark vanishes into the face. What makes relief read is darkness in the field beside the shape, plus a small lift. Both are fakes. Both are mandatory.

  • The dark run must be long

    Metal spends most of its surface in shadow and earns its colour in a narrow band. My first ramp was weighted toward its own mid tone and rendered as orange plastic.

  • Height fields blur in float

    Round-tripping through 8-bit quantises the field, and a quantised field differentiates into visible concentric rings. That artefact is what made the first coin look like a cheap render.

  • Ramps come from tokens.css

    Every stop is a token — graphite-void, bronze-shade, bronze, bronze-hi, edge. Nothing in these images is a colour I picked by eye.

The ceiling held

The gate caught me.

The first cut-paper plate used a disc at reference scale. Your own ceiling rule, already built into check-plate.py, rejected it:

plate                 chroma    dark   peak      verdict
first attempt      35.4%   56.9%     73      chroma coverage 35% > 25%
papercut-night    20.7%   71.6%     73      PASS
papercut-day      17.7%   74.0%     60      PASS

The disc is now sized to the budget rather than to taste, and the composition is better for it — a smaller disc that the bird breaks the edge of beats a large one that contains everything. Peak saturation still is not a failure condition. Coverage is the ceiling; chroma is unbounded, exactly as you set it.

What I filed

Your five references are now a term.

struck is in the lexicon, with all five images analysed and the mechanics extracted. Say the word from now on and it resolves to this, not to a generic idea of texture.

  • Borrowed · the aperture

    A ring that stops containing and becomes an absence, with a world behind the page.

  • Borrowed · layered cut paper

    Depth from N sheets at N offsets under one light. No perspective, no atmosphere, no gradient.

  • Borrowed · blind deboss

    Material revealed by light alone.

  • Not borrowed · the saturated red

    At reference scale it blows the ceiling. Ember is permitted inside imagery — a struck plate is imagery — but the coverage budget still binds.

  • Not borrowed · torii, blossom, hanko, Fuji

    Your references reach for Japan as decor. This brand's Japanese layer is principle and surface. A torii gate in the mark would be tourism.

  • Not borrowed · the glossy bevel

    Three of the five sit close to it. It is the exact failure mode this whole term exists to avoid.

Open

Where I'd like your eye.

  • Which material is the identity?

    My read: cut paper is the mark, foil on dark stock is the application, and the aperture is the site. The coin is a beautiful object but it is a piece of collateral, not a logo.

  • Should the crane become a real fold?

    The cut-paper version implies the geometry could be rebuilt as proper origami facets — five or six planes with true value breaks — rather than four flat shapes plus a crease line. That is a redraw, and it would be the right one.

  • How far does the aperture go?

    It can be the whole homepage hero: the ring as a hole in the page with the garden moving behind it. That is site-design mode, and it is waiting on your word.

  • The wordmark is still unargued

    Archivo at 300 with wide tracking was a round-one proposal that has never been defended. It is now the oldest unexamined thing in the system.
